draft.title: Emotions and motivations
card: A motivation is the reason a character acts. It is often driven by an emotion such as fear, love, guilt, pride or hope.
Writers rarely state a motivation outright. They make it visible through what a character does, says, thinks or avoids.
Example: Tariq throws away the letter, then pulls it from the bin and smooths it flat. The reader sees that he wants to forget it but cannot.
To explain a motivation, name the emotion, point to the detail that shows it, and say what it tells us about why the character acts.
draft.remember: Find the emotion behind the action, then show the detail that reveals it.

a.q: Which sentence best explains a character's motivation?
opts: Guilt drives Lena to leave money on her neighbour's step
Lena leaves money on her neighbour's step at night
Lena is a person who does many unusual things
The writer uses a short sentence when Lena walks home
a.why: It names an emotion, guilt, and links it to an action to give the reason Lena acts. The second option only describes the action. The last option names a technique but gives no reason.
a.clue: Look for the option that gives a reason for the action.

b.q: In a story, Ravi tells everyone he does not care about the race. He stays up late tying his running shoes and checking the start time again and again. What do these details most likely reveal?
opts: His hope of winning, which he hides behind pride
His relief that the race has been cancelled
His anger at the people who asked about it
His boredom with a race he has run before
b.why: His words say he does not care, but his actions show he cares a great deal. The details point to hope, hidden by pride. Anger is tempting because he is defensive, but nothing in his actions shows it.
b.clue: Compare what Ravi says with what he does.

a.best: Guilt drives Lena to leave money on her neighbour's step

b.best: His hope of winning, which he hides behind pride
